summary: SELTRACK backend API tested end-to-end via pytest against the public preview URL. 25/25 tests passed (100%). Covered: root, staff seeding + create, meta denominations, full shift lifecycle (open/close/current), transactions (IN/OUT/ADJUSTMENT + validation), X-report, Z-report (open-shift rejection + closed-shift success), shifts list ordering, get-by-id, daily report, receipt-number monotonicity, and ISO datetime format. All business rules verified — 1760 opening amount from denomination math, running balance = 2010, variance=0 close, negative amount allowed only for ADJUSTMENT, second open blocked with 400, txn without open shift blocked with 400.

minor.issue: Returns HTTP 200 instead of 201 on create (FastAPI default). Not a bug per spec but conventionally 201 Created is preferred.

Uses lexicographic string comparison on ISO timestamps with '+00:00' suffix; works today for UTC dates but if any shift ever stores a non-UTC offset the date-range filter will silently miss/include rows. Consider storing raw datetime with an index, or normalizing to UTC before comparing.

No validation that closing staff_id exists in staff before running compute_expected? Actually it does check 404. OK. However closing note logic uses payload.note or shift.get('note') via shift dict lookup — works but subtle.
FastAPI on_event is deprecated in favor of lifespan handlers (works but deprecation warning in newer versions).

action_items: None — all 25 backend tests pass. Minor code-quality suggestions above are non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single 373-line file — still under the 700-line threshold, but as more features arrive (CSV/PDF export, drawer log, printer session), split into routers/ (staff.py, shifts.py, transactions.py, reports.py) and services/ (compute_expected, receipt counter).
compute_expected() and the identical aggregation block inside current_shift() duplicate the totals aggregation — extract a single helper get_shift_totals(shift_id) returning (totals, expected).
X-report and Z-report have near-identical body construction — extract a build_report(shift, txns, report_type) helper (DRY).

Transactions endpoint stores signed amount as-is (positive for IN/OUT/ADJUSTMENT, negative allowed only for ADJUSTMENT). compute_expected then does opening + IN - OUT + ADJUSTMENT. This is correct, but the sign convention is subtle and undocumented; add a short docstring.
next_receipt_number() is a global counter across all shifts. If daily/shift-scoped receipt numbering is desired for physical receipts, revisit — otherwise fine.
No index on shifts.status or transactions.shift_id — will slow down as data grows. Add MongoDB indexes on startup.
CORS uses '*' by default which is fine for preview; restrict in production.
No pagination metadata on GET /api/shifts or GET /api/transactions (only a raw limit) — consider returning total count for UI paging.
test_credentials: None required — no auth on any endpoint.
seed_data_creation: Server auto-seeds 4 default staff (Rahul Sharma, Priya Patel, Amit Kumar, Sneha Iyer) on first /api/staff hit. Tests additionally created one TEST_Extra Cashier staff record and two shifts (one closed by test flow, one closed by receipt-monotonic sub-test). Preview DB now contains these leftover shifts/txns — safe to leave.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run tests serially with `pytest backend/tests/test_seltrack_backend.py -n 0`. The shared preview DB has state from this run (closed shifts + TEST_Extra Cashier staff). The `_fresh_state` session-scoped fixture closes any lingering open shift at start/end. If pytest-xdist parallelism (>1 worker) is left enabled, TestShiftFlow will race — hence the -n 0 requirement. Frontend was intentionally skipped (backend-only request).
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional issues. During the first parallel run, 3 tests appeared to fail (X-report 404, Z-report 200 instead of 400, close 'no open shift'). Root cause: pytest-xdist workers each run the session-scoped `_fresh_state` autouse fixture, and the second worker's teardown ran `_close_any_open_shift` while the first worker was mid-flow. Rerunning with `-n 0` (serial) resulted in 25/25 pass.
